title: Chosen normalized finite compact-support action
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $K_0$ a field in which $\ell$ is invertible, and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type morphism between finite-type $K_0$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Fix a compactification $c$ and the integral and rational values of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. For a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, let $P_E(F)$ be exactly the integral-functor predicate of [lem-weil-compact-support-representative-independence], after its specified strict tower, evaluations, derived-limit functor, unit and Roos projections have been chosen. It retains integral additivity and linearity, literal value equalities, and the projection-preserving natural identification with that fixed strict-tower realization. Define $F_E$ by that existential with predicate $P_E$. This is the already normalized functor, rather than a new arbitrary action on its objects.

Using the raw scalar localization of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], define $G_E$ on objects by the integral output of $F_E$ and on every Hom by the scalar extension of the integral linear map: $a\otimes v\mapsto a\otimes F_E(v)$. This map preserves identities and composition. The integral output is the literal integral compact-support value. For $n\geq0$, define $r_{E,n}$ to be the tensor/restriction adjunct of the very $n$-th Roos projection used in the chosen integral compact-support value, using the adjunction of [lem-weil-derived-scalar-extension-restriction-adjunction] and the tower of [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower]. This adjunct is invertible. Transport it along the integral value equality to obtain the fixed reduction isomorphism for $F_E$.

source.place: Tensor reassociation, compact-support reduction, and transported coefficient comparisons; used in finite-field-independence proof step 1

proof.text: Project the specified integral-functor existential from compact-support representative independence. Its chosen witness supplies additivity, integral linearity and the literal object equalities.
The Hom map is baseChange of the integral linear Hom map. Prove identity and composition on pure tensors using the functor laws and the prescribed tensor composition, and extend by tensor induction.

Take a simultaneous coefficient reduction calculus and apply the native open-extension and proper-image system functors. Compare its evaluations and transitions with the specified compact-support quotient maps. Identify the sequence-site and direct-quotient transitions by their identical horizontal section formula.

The input iterated-reduction adjunct beta is invertible by the quotient cocycle theorem. Its source is constructible because it is isomorphic to the next reduction of the input. Factor the output transition adjunct as the finite compact-support scalar comparison followed by compact support of beta. Both factors are invertible. Adjunction and the evaluation isomorphisms therefore prove normalization of the native output system.

Apply the normalized coefficient-sequence Roos model and generic normalized DVR Roos finite-reduction theorem. The auxiliary finite-field datum is independent of the schemes and only supplies the generic coefficient convention. Thus the total-system-limit projection adjunct is invertible without a finite-base-field or Tor assumption.

Transport the native strict-tower Roos triangle through the evaluation isomorphisms to the exact sfCompactSupportTerm and sfCompactSupportTransition tower. Compare this triangle with the chosen defining Roos triangle by rotation and the triangle five lemma. The resulting vertex isomorphism preserves the product projection. Adjunction naturality expresses the chosen projection adjunct as reduced vertex isomorphism, the already invertible total-system-limit adjunct and the finite evaluation isomorphism.
